summary: PR #1969, analyst reconstruction. Baseline e7073368fcd87fb5be224b6bb7971a55f5316f40. Reuses #1724, #1616, #1882, #1964, #1965 and the open #1966. The note docs/notes/unique-feedback-explanation-311.md, Closed-cone selection without a quantitative transfer ledger, gives an unregistered set-theoretic deduction: for a monotone activation operator on the actual roster, the uniform guard that every derived activation needs an active actual supplier ensures the complement U of a rootless supplier-closed cone is prefixed. Union of the postfixed substates in U yields its greatest fixed substate; an independently nonempty outside postfixed witness makes that fixed substate populated. Thus a non-deletion criterion for the cone among relevant fixed substates excludes a rootless cone under the explicit guards, without global well-foundedness, receipt exclusivity or a quantitative measure. The targeted cone-intersection criterion is weaker than whole-configuration uniqueness. An unconditional outside root plus an acyclic infinite chain admits the fixed states {s} and the full order, so global nonemptiness and root existence do not guarantee CCR. A nonmonotone finite control shows why the restricted fixed-point existence assumption matters. Exhaustive Python diagnostic over 74088 eligible three-node operator/relation pairs checked 15317 cone cases and 450 with a populated outside postfixed witness. Structural controls only; no modal world or real production certified. Strongest surviving denial offers a bearerless necessary or primitive global constitutive fact with independent existential import; an underived concrete whole supplying its parts concedes the relative root. Existing root/common-source and necessity/uniqueness connections are mapped with their separate premises. Prior conditional modest preference and unrestricted underdetermination are retained, no change to reviewed current assessments or formal closure. Evidence is draft research, not a registered result.
